title: Emrys and the Autopsy
premise: Elodie Sterling, a reclusive estate lawyer with a private habit of solving deaths the police mislabel as accidents, is summoned to read the will of a wealthy matriarch—a will that legally cannot exist because she was declared dead two years ago. When a second body appears dressed in clothes stolen from Elodie's own closet, he realizes someone is staging him as either suspect or next victim, using details only available in sealed case files. As Elodie races to decode the forged will's hidden cipher, he uncovers a conspiracy reaching into the coroner's office and his own past, forcing him to choose between protecting the one person who ever made him feel he belonged and exposing a truth that will destroy them both. In the end, Elodie traps the killer—the autopsy technician who faked the matriarch's first death—by letting himself be framed, clearing his name at the cost of the belonging he'd finally found.
about_author: Xanthe Okafor spent a decade as a probate paralegal in coastal New England before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange human dramas hidden inside estate files. She writes mysteries about quiet people who notice too much, and lives with an uncooperative cat named Verdict.

chapters.title: The Will That Couldn't Be
chapters.summary: Elodie Sterling, POV. Summoned to Blackthorn House to read the will of Vivienne Marsh—declared dead two years prior. The document is flawless, notarized, impossible. Elodie's unease sharpens into professional fascination. Emotional beat: the thrill of an anomaly meeting the dread of being watched.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter establishing Elodie's secret history: three 'accidental' deaths he quietly proved were murders, never credited. His mentor, retired Detective Ruth Calloway, warns him this new case feels staged. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: loneliness of a man whose gift isolates him.

chapters.title: The Beneficiaries
chapters.summary: The will names four heirs: estranged son Aldous, caretaker Mara Voss, a charity—and a fifth beneficiary listed only as 'E. Sterling.' Elodie realizes he's been written into a dead woman's testament. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: violation; the case has chosen him personally.

chapters.title: Blackthorn House
chapters.summary: Elodie investigates the decaying estate, finding Vivienne's study preserved like a shrine and fresh footprints in dust. He meets Mara, the caretaker, who seems to know more than she says. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: creeping intimacy with a place that feels designed for him.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Aldous Marsh is found dead in the boathouse, wearing Elodie's stolen overcoat and carrying Elodie's fountain pen. Police pivot toward Elodie as suspect. POV alternates Elodie and Detective Imani Reyes, who remembers his name from an old file. Emotional beat: exposure—his invisibility is gone.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Reyes confronts Elodie privately; he shows her his method on the three old cases, earning wary alliance instead of handcuffs. She reveals the crime scene was arranged from sealed autopsy records. POV: dual Elodie/Reyes. Emotional beat: cautious trust forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Sealed Files
chapters.summary: Elodie traces who accessed the coroner's archives: a short list including autopsy technician Dr. Pavel Brandt, who signed off on Vivienne Marsh's original death certificate. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the killer reads the same documents he does.

chapters.title: Mara's Story
chapters.summary: Mara confesses she helped Vivienne fake her death two years ago to escape Aldous's financial abuse—but swears the current killer isn't her. Elodie believes her, mostly. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: belonging—he recognizes a fellow invisible person.

chapters.title: The Cipher
chapters.summary: Elodie discovers the impossible will contains a hidden acrostic pointing to Vivienne's real location and a warning: 'the one who signs the dead.' He realizes the will itself is a message from beyond a grave that may be empty. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Brandt
chapters.summary: Elodie interviews Dr. Brandt, charming and meticulous, who explains away every discrepancy with plausible ease. Only afterward does Elodie realize Brandt quoted a detail from a file that was never unsealed. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the cold certainty of having shaken hands with the killer.

chapters.title: Second Death Certificate
chapters.summary: Aldous's autopsy lists cause of death as cardiac arrest—before any autopsy occurred. The paperwork was pre-written. Reyes pulls strings to get the raw report; it matches Brandt's handwriting habits. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: institutional rot; the system itself is compromised.

chapters.title: What Ruth Knew
chapters.summary: Ruth Calloway reveals that years ago she investigated a falsified autopsy ring and was forced into retirement for pursuing it. Brandt was her prime suspect then. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: vindication and grief—an old wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Trap That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Elodie and Reyes set a trap using leaked false information, but the killer anticipates it perfectly—someone inside the investigation is feeding him everything. Suspicion falls on Reyes's junior officer. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: paranoia; no channel is clean.

chapters.title: Vivienne Alive
chapters.summary: Following the cipher, Elodie finds Vivienne Marsh living incognito in a coastal cottage—alive, sharp, and terrified. She confirms Brandt faked her death for a fee, then began killing everyone who could expose the scheme. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by dread—she is bait now too.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Vivienne begs Elodie to stay silent; exposure destroys her freedom and ruins Mara. Elodie faces the choice: protect the small circle that has accepted him, or tell the truth and save future victims. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—belonging versus truth.

chapters.title: The Missing Night
chapters.summary: Reyes discovers gaps in the surveillance logs the night Aldous died—gaps Brandt couldn't have created alone. Someone else is complicit. Elodie suspects Mara lied about one crucial hour. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: betrayal surfacing inside the fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Confession at the Cottage
chapters.summary: Mara admits she tipped off Brandt about Aldous's visit—not knowing he intended murder—to protect Vivienne's secret. Elodie must decide whether her lie damns her. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: compassion wrestling with justice.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Elodie proposes the endgame: he will publicly announce he's found Vivienne alive, forcing Brandt to come finish the job. Reyes objects; Elodie insists the trap needs living bait, and volunteers himself. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: resolve—the invisible man choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: The Autopsy Theater
chapters.summary: The trap springs at the county morgue after hours, where Brandt comes to destroy evidence and finds Elodie waiting among the steel tables. Brandt nearly turns the frame back onto Elodie until Reyes arrives with the handwriting evidence. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terror and clarity intertwined—the climax.

chapters.title: Signed by the Dead
chapters.summary: Brandt confesses with chilling professionalism, explaining how he turned death certification into a business. Reyes arrests him; the complicit records clerk is exposed. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: grim satisfaction—systems can be beaten by patient people.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: The legal aftermath: Vivienne must publicly die again, truly this time; Mara faces reduced charges; Elodie drafts the honest version of the will. He declines credit, but Reyes tells the press anyway. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: bittersweet recognition—he can't be invisible anymore.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Final chapter reveals the meaning of the title: 'E. Sterling' in the will stood for Emrys, the name Vivienne gave Elodie in the cipher—Welsh for 'ambassador,' one who carries messages between worlds, living and dead. He accepts a standing consultancy with Reyes and keeps Mara's friendship. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth, not silence.
